PERSPECTIVE / ASM FORMALISATION

What makes formal participation worth choosing?

Formalisation is more likely to endure when participants can see a viable economic pathway.

BELDIUM PERSPECTIVES · OCTOBER 2026 · ADVISORY COMMENTARY

Start with the participant’s decision

A formalisation framework asks people to change how they work. The useful question is not only what the state requires, but what miners need in order to participate consistently. Registration costs, travel, administrative complexity and market conditions all belong in the diagnostic.

Connect recognition to opportunity

Legal recognition should be examined alongside production records, safety, quality assurance and routes to formal buyers. These elements do not automatically produce better livelihoods, but together they define a more credible proposition than registration alone.

Design for institutional feasibility

A pathway must also be deliverable by the institutions responsible for it. Responsibilities, verification arrangements, capacity needs and monitoring should be explicit. A realistic pilot can test assumptions before a wider rollout.

This perspective presents an analytical approach. It is not a report of a completed assignment or a country-specific assessment.
